kind: analytic bound — NOT a measurement on a classic-scrollbar platform

control.what: every row re-derived at the matrix's own 0px scrollbar and compared against the browser's measurement; surface +/-0.01px, content +/-0.5px (content_px is rounded in the artifact), gate exact

not_covered: the @media gutter bands: a classic bar moves the 767px/479px edges to 782px/494px of CSS viewport, and no swept width lands in either 15px window — the gutter is held fixed here

the width-bucket stamp: bucket(window.innerWidth) reads a scrollbar-INCLUSIVE width while @media/@container read a scrollbar-EXCLUSIVE one, so the two disagree by the scrollbar width near every edge on a classic platform; only the CSS side is modelled
scrollbar widths other than the one passed in
anything a classic platform changes that is not the layout viewport (font stack, DPI rounding)

reachability.note: this swept width clears the gate by 95px, so 915px is an UPPER bound on where the gate first opens, not the edge itself
this swept width sits EXACTLY on the gate (720.0px), so the shift is exact: 764px of CSS viewport becomes 779px on a 15px classic bar
